question.text: The SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations require listed companies to:

answer.text: Make timely disclosures of material events, publish financial results quarterly, and maintain corporate governance standards
Only disclose information to preferred investors
Only publish information when SEBI specifically requests it

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations impose a continuous-disclosure regime on listed companies. Listed entities are required to publish periodic (quarterly and annual) financial results, make timely disclosure of material events and price-sensitive information, and comply with prescribed corporate-governance standards (board composition, committees, related-party transactions, etc.). The Trap: Filing only annual returns ignores the periodic and event-based disclosure regime. Disclosure to "preferred investors" only would violate the fair-disclosure principle. Companies cannot wait for SEBI to specifically request information — much of the regime is proactive. Note: The NISM Series XV (Research Analyst) workbook pages reviewed support fair disclosure, UPSI, governance standards, and periodic financial statements as concepts, but the LODR-specific framing of "timely disclosure of material events" together with quarterly results and governance was not found in the workbook pages reviewed. The framing above is presented as general SEBI listed-company-regulation industry knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
